question: Does full cold-process mixed XOR extraction+native CMS significantly improve bounded solve completion versus untouched original-CNF CryptoMiniSat, CaDiCaL195, Glucose4 when baseline CPU cap increases from 8s to 30s? Source already seen; development calibration ONLY, not independent science.
locked_algorithm: Existing exact source-sign-mask extractor 004D4 and fixed solver versions (pycryptosat==5.15.0, python-sat==1.9.dev17) unchanged; all original CNF and extracted clause count reverified. None of the 004D6 rank-zero redundant equations added.

comparability.full_wall: Subprocess Python cold startup + import + original source hash & DIMACS + parse + optional XOR extraction + solver init/add + solve + full original SAT model validation
comparability.full_CPU: process_time includes all of the same operations; CPU and wall use distinct units and never compared as ratios
comparability.source_model: Known separately archived full SAT assignment, original instance SAT, so every UNSAT verdict is an ERROR not a success
comparability.interpreter: Record whether solved under each budget, total cold-run CPU, end-to-end wall, max RSS, std; all failures and timeouts included; no finite ratio from censored trials; no generalization or significance from single source.
